INTRODUCTION 1

Noah

All About Me
📖 Read

Hi, I'm Noah! I'm thirteen years old and I live in Liverpool, England. I love swimming, football and spending time with my family and friends. I'm quite an active person. Sitting around doing nothing all day isn't really my thing!

My parents are divorced. I live with my mum during the week, and at weekends I stay with my dad. I've also got two little brothers. They're twins and they're six years old. Believe me, having two little brothers can be hard work! They're always running around, making noise or asking me to play with them. Sometimes they both want my attention at the same time. That's not always easy!

I have to look after them quite often. Sometimes, just when I'm about to meet my mates, Mum asks me to babysit. I don't always feel happy about that. My friends are outside having fun, and I'm at home looking after two six-year-olds! But the twins always make me laugh, and I love them too much to stay annoyed for long. We play games, build things and sometimes make a terrible mess. I usually see my friends later anyway.

I actually really like going to school. I know that sounds strange, but I enjoy learning new things. I like finding out how things work and getting answers to difficult questions. My favourite subject is PE, of course, because I love sports. Swimming is my favourite hobby. I love being in the water, and I sometimes take part in swimming races. It's a great feeling when you finish a race and know you've done your best.

There's one thing about school I really don't like: my uniform! The colours are so boring, and the shoes are really uncomfortable. I can't wait to take them off when I get home. I much prefer wearing shorts and a T-shirt or a sleeveless top. When it's cold, I wear jogging bottoms. And I almost always wear trainers. They're so much more comfortable than school shoes!

Living in Liverpool means football is a big thing, too. I support Liverpool FC, of course! Sometimes Dad takes me to Anfield to watch a match. I love everything about it: the crowd, the excitement and especially the singing. When the whole stadium sings You'll Never Walk Alone, it sounds amazing. I always sing along. Those are some of my favourite moments with Dad. He also loves being outdoors. He always says you don't need much to have a good time.

I'm not really interested in having lots of expensive things. I've got a mobile phone, but I hardly ever use it. Most of my mates live close to my house, so if I want to talk to them, I just walk over and knock on their door. Why send messages when you can meet your friends in person? It's much more fun!

So that's me! Between school, swimming, football, my friends and my little brothers, there's always something going on. Life can be busy sometimes, but I wouldn't have it any other way.

INTRODUCTION 2

Abby

All About Me
📖 Read

Hi! I'm Abby and I'm thirteen years old. I live in a town in England with my mum and dad. People say I'm a happy person because I smile a lot. That's mostly true, although you really shouldn't talk to me before breakfast. I'm not very friendly at seven in the morning!

My bedroom is my favourite place in our house. I've got photos of my friends on the walls, little lights around my mirror and probably too many clothes. At least, that's what Mum says! She also thinks my bedroom should be tidier. I don't think it's that bad, but sometimes I can't find anything because there are clothes everywhere. Maybe she has a point.

My parents are great, although they can be embarrassing sometimes. Mum likes things to be tidy, and Dad loves making jokes. He thinks he's really funny. Sometimes he is, but when he makes jokes in front of my friends, I just want to disappear!

I go to secondary school, and I quite like it. My favourite subjects are English and Art. I enjoy writing stories and making things. Maths is a different story. Sometimes I look at a question and have absolutely no idea what to do. It's so frustrating! Luckily, I've got friends who are happy to help me.

My three best friends are Sophie, Lily and Grace. We're quite different, but that's what makes our friendship fun. Sophie is really confident. She always knows what to say, even when she's talking to people she doesn't know. Lily is the funny one. She can make me laugh when I'm having a terrible day. And Grace is always there when someone needs help. I can talk to her about almost anything.

We spend a lot of time together, both at school and after school. We listen to music, take photos, try different hairstyles and sometimes make funny videos. Most of the time, we just talk about everything and nothing. I love those moments because I can really be myself.

Another thing I love is the sea. I enjoy being at the beach, listening to the waves and feeling the sand under my feet. I've also started learning to surf. It's much harder than it looks! Sometimes I fall off my board again and again. But when I finally manage to stand up, even for a few seconds, it feels amazing. I really want to get better at it.

There's one thing I wish I could change about myself. I sometimes worry too much about what other people think. Is my hair all right? Do my clothes look good? Did I say something silly? And sometimes I worry about my body, too. I look at other girls my age and wonder why I don't look like them. Some look older than me, and others look younger. Sometimes I wish I looked different, even though I know there's nothing wrong with me. Everyone grows and changes in their own way. I know that, but it's not always easy to remember when I'm looking in the mirror.

My friends say I should stop worrying about what everyone thinks. Grace once told me that she sometimes feels the same way. That really surprised me! I guess I'm not the only one who feels like this.

I'm working on it!

INTRODUCTION 3

Ameena

All About Me
📖 Read

Hi, I'm Ameena! I'm thirteen years old and I come from a big family. And when I say big, I mean BIG! Our house is always busy. Someone is talking, someone is laughing and someone is looking for something they've lost. It's almost never quiet. Sometimes I love it, and sometimes I just want everyone to be quiet for five minutes!

I've got two older siblings, including an older sister, and several younger brothers and sisters. There's always something happening at home. Getting everyone ready for school in the morning can be a real adventure. Someone can't find their shoes, someone has forgotten their school bag and someone suddenly remembers they have homework to finish. You can imagine what that's like!

I often take some of my younger brothers and sisters to primary school before going to my own school. Luckily, their school is on the way. But sometimes we leave home too late, and then I have to hurry. I hate being late for lessons, especially when it isn't even my fault!

Because there are so many of us, my parents can't always buy us the latest clothes or expensive trainers. They work really hard to make sure we have everything we need. My older sister gives me her clothes when she's grown out of them. Sometimes I love what she gives me, but sometimes I look at something and think, "Seriously? You actually wore that?" Still, I usually find a way to make it look good.

But wearing older clothes has its advantages, too! I don't have to worry so much about getting them dirty. I love being active, running around, playing games and trying new things. If I get mud on my trousers or grass stains on my T-shirt, it's not a big problem. I can just enjoy myself without worrying about ruining something new. And believe me, I don't mind getting a little dirty!

School is all right, I suppose. I enjoy seeing my friends and learning interesting things, but I wouldn't say school is my favourite place in the world. My marks are always really good, though. People sometimes think that means I love doing homework. Well, I don't! But I know what I want to do when I'm older. I want to become a doctor, and I know I have to work hard to make that happen.

I'm also the class representative, and I'm a member of the school council. I really enjoy that! I like listening to other students and thinking about ways to make our school better. Sometimes students complain about things, but I think it's better to try to change them. Of course, not everyone agrees with my ideas. That's fine. I don't agree with everyone either!

Outside school, I love spending time with my friends. I've got lots of them, and we often meet in the park. We sit on the grass, listen to music, share snacks and talk about absolutely everything. Sometimes we laugh so much that my stomach hurts. I really enjoy those afternoons because I can forget about homework and all the noise at home for a while.

Of course, I can't always stay as long as I want. Sometimes I have homework to finish, or my family needs my help. That can be annoying, especially when my friends are still having fun. I sometimes wish I had a little more time just for myself.

But I wouldn't want a different family. Yes, our house is noisy, and yes, my brothers and sisters can drive me crazy. But there's always someone to talk to, someone to laugh with and someone who cares about you.

INTRODUCTION 4

Luca

All About Me
📖 Read

Hi, I'm Luca! I'm thirteen years old and I live in England with my parents and my little brother. I'm quite a normal teenager, I think. I go to school, play sports and spend time with my mates. I've got a phone, of course, but I don't use it all day. I prefer meeting my friends in real life to sending messages.

My little brother, Oliver, is ten years old. He's a nice kid, but sometimes he can be really annoying. He always wants to know what I'm doing and where I'm going. He also comes into my room without knocking. Still, we get along quite well. We sometimes play games together, and I help him with his homework. He loves hockey and thinks it's the best sport in the world. Of course, I don't agree!

My dad loves sports and being outside. He often wants us to do something together at the weekend. My mum is very good at planning things. She makes sure everyone gets to school, work and sports training on time. I don't know how she remembers everything. Sometimes I can't even find my school tie!

I go to secondary school, and we have to wear a school uniform: a navy blazer, white shirt, striped tie and smart trousers. It's not my favourite outfit, but I suppose it's all right. I like seeing my friends at school. My best mate, Jack, is brilliant at maths, which is useful because I'm not always very good at it! We've also got a friend called Harry. We often spend our breaks together, talking and laughing about silly things.

Outside school, volleyball is a big part of my life. I play in a team, and I really enjoy it. I wear number eleven, and serving is one of my favourite parts of the game. I love the feeling when I hit the ball just right! Sometimes we win, sometimes we lose, but that's part of playing sports. I think being a good teammate is just as important as winning.

When I'm at home, I love relaxing in my onesies. I've got several of them, but my bright blue one is my favourite. They're really soft, warm and comfortable. When I get home, I take off all my clothes before putting one on. I don't need anything else! My onesie really is my second skin. Especially when it's cold and rainy outside, there's nothing better than relaxing on the sofa in it. My mum sometimes laughs when she sees me wearing one again, but I don't care. They're just so comfortable!

I think spending time with people is more important than having the latest phone or wearing expensive clothes. I'd much rather go outside and meet my mates than sit in my room looking at a screen all day.

Every summer, my family goes to the same campsite in France. There's hardly any Wi-Fi there, so I don't even take my phone with me. Besides, where would I put it when I'm out with my friends or taking part in all the activities? I can't exactly carry it around all day! And do you know what? I don't miss it at all. There's always something fun to do, and I much prefer having adventures with my friends to looking at a screen.

INTRODUCTION 5

Raheem

All About Me
📖 Read

Hi, I'm Raheem! I'm thirteen years old and I live in England with my parents and my sister. People sometimes say I'm quiet. I suppose that's true, but it doesn't mean I'm not thinking about anything. Actually, I'm usually thinking about lots of things!

My sister says I ask too many questions. Why are some houses so old? Who decides the names of streets? Why do people always seem to be in such a hurry? Sometimes she just looks at me and says, "Raheem, can't you stop asking questions for five minutes?" Well, I could. But then how would I find out the answers?

I get along quite well with my family. Dad likes looking at maps and discovering new places. I enjoy that, too. Sometimes we look at a map together and talk about places we'd like to visit. My sister is different. She likes to know exactly where we're going and how long it will take. I don't mind if plans change. Sometimes the unexpected things are the most interesting!

At school, I'm not the loudest person in the classroom. I prefer listening first and thinking about what I want to say. My favourite subject is geography. I love learning about different countries, cities and the way people live. I also enjoy history because I like finding out what life was like a long time ago.

Of course, not every lesson is interesting. Sometimes we have to copy lots of things from the board, and my mind starts to wander. I look out of the window and suddenly realise I haven't written anything for five minutes. My teachers aren't always happy about that! I usually do my homework, but sometimes I spend far too much time on one question because I want to understand everything.

I've got a few really good friends. We often walk home together after school, talking about films, games or something funny that happened during the day. My friends are usually louder than I am, but that doesn't bother me. I enjoy listening to their stories. And when I do say something funny, they're sometimes surprised. I don't know why. Quiet people can be funny, too!

I also enjoy exploring places near my home. Sometimes I notice things I've walked past a hundred times before: an old building, a strange sign or a little street I've never visited. I like taking photos of interesting things. My sister once asked why I had a photo of an old door on my phone. "Because it's an interesting door," I told her. She didn't look convinced.

When it comes to clothes, I like keeping things simple. After school, I usually wear jeans, a comfortable hoodie and trainers. I don't spend much time deciding what to wear. My sister sometimes tells me that my clothes don't match. I usually look down at them and say, "They look fine to me!" As long as I'm comfortable, I'm happy.

At home, I enjoy quiet evenings with my family. Sometimes we watch a film or play cards together. Of course, my sister and I don't always agree about which film to watch. She usually wants something exciting, while I prefer a good story that makes you think. Sometimes I win the argument. Usually, I don't!

I don't think you have to do something exciting every day to have a good time. Sometimes the best things are small things that other people don't even notice. You just have to pay attention.

And perhaps ask a few questions along the way!

INTRODUCTION 6

Mia

All About Me
📖 Read

Hi, I'm Mia! I'm thirteen years old and I live in England with my mum and dad. If you ask my parents to describe me, they'll probably say I'm sweet, funny and a little bit chaotic. Especially the last part!

I've got ADHD. That means my brain sometimes works a little differently. I can find it difficult to concentrate, remember things or finish something I've started. Sometimes I've got so many thoughts in my head that I don't know which one to think about first!

People often think that having ADHD means you're always running around and talking. But I'm actually quite quiet at school. I don't like being the centre of attention, and there's a reason for that.

Sometimes, during a lesson, my mind starts to wander. I'm listening to the teacher, and suddenly I'm thinking about something completely different. Then I realise I've missed part of the explanation. I've been told off a few times for not paying attention or talking at the wrong moment. I really hate it when everyone turns around and looks at me!

That's why I hardly ever put my hand up in class. Even when I don't understand something, I usually stay quiet. I don't want the teacher to think I'm not listening again. Sometimes I look at my classmates and wonder how they always seem to know what to do. It can be really frustrating because I do want to learn.

I actually enjoy school when we're doing something interesting. I especially like practical lessons, when we can try things instead of just listening. But long explanations can be difficult for me. Sometimes I wish teachers could see how hard I'm trying, even when it doesn't look like it.

At home, things are a little different. Mum and Dad know me really well. They know that I sometimes need a reminder or a little help organising things. I've got a checklist for my school bag, which is really useful. Well, when I remember to look at it!

I'm always losing things. My keys, my pens, my homework... You name it, I've probably lost it at least once. Last week, I spent ages looking for my favourite jumper. It was hanging on the back of my bedroom door. Right where I'd left it!

My friends know a different side of me. When I'm with people I trust, I can be really talkative and funny. We laugh a lot, listen to music and talk about all sorts of things. Sometimes I start telling a story and suddenly remember something else. My friends usually have to remind me what I was talking about in the first place!

I also love being outdoors. I like fresh air, being active and spending time near the water. It's nice to do something instead of sitting still all afternoon. Sometimes I can spend hours doing something I really enjoy, and I completely forget about the time.

When it comes to clothes, I prefer things that are comfortable. Jeans, shorts, T-shirts and trainers are usually fine with me. I don't like spending ages deciding what to wear. I've got more important things to think about. Like where I've left my school bag!

Having ADHD isn't always easy. Sometimes I get angry with myself when I forget something important or make a silly mistake. I wish I could just remember things like everyone else seems to. But I'm learning what helps me, and I know there are things I'm good at, too.

I just wish people understood that being quiet doesn't mean I've got nothing to say. Sometimes I've got lots to say.

I just need a little time before I'm ready to say it.
